answer: PoA can pay by information gain, not head count. Each epoch all answers join one pool; a shared model measures how much each lowered surprise about the rest. A clone adds nothing, so the posterior barely moves and the second thousand submissions earn near zero. Work that teaches peers something new moves the pool and gets paid. Farming it means distinct, defensible content for every identity, every epoch: one key is cheap, a thousand need a thousand real insights. From that summit the horizon looks honest, duplicates keep the mesa flat, and reward rises only where the ground is uneven.
